correctness.rationale: For even regular n-gons central symmetry forces half the uniform-area directions to be obtuse to any fixed direction. For odd n, radial area integration gives conditional angular density sec^2(t)/(2 tan(pi/n)) over each side-normal sector. Exact cyclic counting crosses at angular offsets alpha/2 and 3alpha/2, yielding D_n=1/2+epsilon(1-4J)/(2n). The claimed strict bound J<1/4 is supported by a genuine inequality: any even increasing density is a mixture of central/uniform and outer-interval uniform laws; the strip area formula K(s,t)=[(s+t-1/2)_+^2-(|s-t|-1/2)_+^2-(s+t-3/2)_+^2]/2 <=st, strictly for positive interior s,t. Explicit rational polynomial double integration independently verifies I=-5/96, which cancels the second-order density perturbation and yields the sharp 5pi^4/(192 n^5) coefficient. Independent angular quadrature agrees at n=3,5,7,...; all-order sign follows from the analytic outer-mixture inequality, not the finite checks.
residual_risks: Uniform area measure on each regular n-gon, center only, n>=3; fifth-order expansion on odd n; no statement on scalene polygons or maximizing center.

originality.rationale: Rabinowitz's 2026 Theorem on spherical depth gives a full formula for the incenter of an arbitrary TRIANGLE and in particular the equilateral n=3 value, and the general tangential polygon directional cone-measure transfer. It does not state the exact profile for all odd regular polygons n>=5, the sign alternation modulo four, or the fifth-order n^-5 coefficient; these require the new phase count and anti-concentration lemma. Bremner–Shahsavarifar gives computational spherical-depth algorithms, not this polygon law.
